title: Data movement — concept map
intro: Moving data between on-premises NFS/SMB shares, other clouds, and Amazon S3 requires choosing the right transfer mechanism. AWS DataSync uses lightweight agents for scheduled or one-time migrations. S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) continuously copies objects for disaster recovery or locality. Batch pipelines (Glue, EMR) suit periodic ETL; streaming (Kinesis, MSK) suits real-time ingestion. Every path needs encryption in transit and at rest plus least-privilege IAM.

conceptCards.title: DataSync
conceptCards.summary: Agent + source/destination locations + task. Incremental, verified transfers with bandwidth limits.
conceptCards.example: 10 TB NAS → S3 with task schedule nightly

conceptCards.title: S3 CRR
conceptCards.summary: Async replication on new objects. Requires versioning on both buckets. RTC option for 15-min SLA.

conceptCards.title: Batch vs streaming
conceptCards.summary: Batch: scheduled ETL, lower cost, higher latency. Streaming: sub-second, operational complexity.
conceptCards.example: Daily sales report = Glue; fraud alerts = Kinesis

conceptCards.title: Security
conceptCards.summary: TLS in transit, SSE-KMS at rest, bucket policies, VPC endpoints, CloudTrail audit.
conceptCards.example: DataSync task role scoped to prefix only
